newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian retailers eye Marks & Spencer.
newsitem.headline: Australian retailers eye Marks & Spencer.

text.p: Leading Australian retailers showed on Tuesday they were keeping a watchful eye on the planned arrival of British chain store Marks & Spencer Plc.

Upmarket department store David Jones Ltd said it was looking at ways in which it might be able to co-operate with the British chain while Australia's largest retailer, Coles Myer Ltd, warned Marks could find the competition tough.
David Jones chairman Dick Warburton, responding to a question at the annual meeting, said the company was "looking at ways and means" of co-operating with Marks.

He later told reporters David Jones had some advantages that it could offer Marks & Spencer, which announced last month that it had targeted Australia for development and would start looking for franchise partners early in 1997.
"Then again they might prefer to go completely separate to ourselves," Warburton said.
"All I am saying is that no bets are off," he said. Asked if David Jones was contemplating a merger, he said: "It doesn't have to be a merger, it could just be some alliance.

Coles Myer chairman Nobby Clark, also responding to a shareholder's question at his company's annual meeting in Sydney, said: "We are looking with a great deal of interest at the advent of Marks and Spencer in this market."
Clark said he understood Marks & Spencer's plans had not been fully formulated, although he believed its move into countries such as Canada had not been substantial.
"We will watch them carefully and learn from them," he said.
However, Clark said he expected Marks and Spencer would find the competition tough in Australia. "Perhaps they won't find the game as easy as in the U.K.," he said.
